title: Yepun on the VLT platform
caption: Yepun and an Auxiliary Telescope on the Very Large Telescope platform
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Two telescopes share this night scene on the platform of ESO's Very Large Telescope. The large one is the fourth Unit Telescope, known as Yepun, and it is sending a laser beam up into the sky. To the right stands a much smaller companion, one of the Auxiliary Telescopes.

The laser creates what astronomers call a guide star. It is part of the telescope's adaptive optics system, which measures how the turbulent air above the site is blurring starlight and corrects for that disturbance. With the blurring removed, the telescope can study the sky in far greater detail than it otherwise could.

The smaller instrument is the second of four Auxiliary Telescopes on the platform, each with a mirror 1.8 meters across. They are modest beside the Unit Telescopes, but they belong to the same observatory and share the same platform.

understand.summary: A ground-based photograph by A. Ghizzi Panizza for ESO, taken in visible light. The colors are those the camera recorded.
understand.eye: A camera exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the laser beam and the night sky may look brighter in the photograph than they would to someone on the platform.

explore: The photograph is credited to A. Ghizzi Panizza for ESO. Adaptive optics is the general name for systems that adjust a telescope's optics to cancel out atmospheric blurring, and the laser guide star gives the system a reference point to measure against.
alt: A large telescope enclosure firing a laser beam into the night sky, with a smaller telescope standing to the right.
